meta.subtitle: Second-quarter 2026 results met or beat guidance, but guided growth slows and the shares sit near their 52-week low, a fall our documents do not explain

advisories: model vs Street expected return diverge by 25pp — informational, not scored

analystSentiment.commentary:
Boston Scientific Corporation reported a second quarter of 2026 that landed at or above its own guidance, yet the shares trade at $42.26, close to the bottom of their 52-week range. Three things keep us from a positive call: the company's July 29, 2026 outlook points to a slower second half, its 10-Q reports new pressure in Electrophysiology and in certain WATCHMAN procedures, and none of the documents we draw on says why the market has marked the stock down.

Our scenarios weight a Base that keeps today's multiple at 55%, a Bear in which earnings stall and the multiple compresses at 25%, and a Bull at the Street's median target at 20%. That gives a probability-weighted fair value of $44.46 and expected upside of +5.2%, close to the price and well short of the return we would need for a positive call against a real bear case. The valuation section argues each anchor and weight, and the final recommendation sets out the price and the evidence that would change the label.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Boston Scientific Corporation describes itself in its 10-Q as "a global developer, manufacturer and marketer of medical devices that are used in a broad range of interventional medical specialties". It is headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts.

The 10-Q MD&A presents net sales by two reportable segments. MedSurg comprises the Endoscopy, Urology and Neuromodulation businesses. Cardiovascular has, since the fourth quarter of 2025, combined the legacy Cardiology and Peripheral Interventions businesses, and its products include the Farapulse Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) System and the AGENT Drug-Coated Balloon. Cardiovascular is the larger segment, with second-quarter 2026 net sales of $3,624 million against $1,818 million for MedSurg.

In the second quarter of 2026, which ended June 30, net sales were $5.442 billion, up 7.5% year over year on a reported basis and 7.0% on an organic basis. Reported diluted EPS was $0.61, against $0.53 a year earlier.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: The case turns on whether FY27 consensus earnings survive the slowdown the company has guided to. If they do, the current price pays a low multiple for a business with high gross margins, strong free cash flow and an active clinical program in its larger segment. If they do not, the multiple is less low than it looks, because the pressure the 10-Q describes falls on businesses that have carried growth. We think consensus is more likely to hold than to break, but not by enough to pay for a re-rating, so our Base keeps today's multiple and our Bear sits well below the price. The catalysts and risks below point to the evidence that would tip the balance.

catalysts: The third-quarter 2026 report will test the company's guidance for approximately 3 to 5 percent reported and organic net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $0.80 to $0.82.
Clinical results the July 29 release reports, including the AVANT GUARD study of FARAPULSE in persistent atrial fibrillation, could support demand if they translate into adoption.
The new global restructuring program the Board approved on July 21, 2026 may lower costs; the 10-Q excerpt gives no size or savings estimate.
The completed $2 billion accelerated share repurchase lowers the share count and supports per-share earnings.
The $1.5 billion MiRus LLC investment carries an exclusive option to acquire the MiRus TAVR business, whose SIEGEL system is still investigational.
risks: The 10-Q says increased competition in Electrophysiology and a deceleration of certain WATCHMAN procedures affected second-quarter sales.
An unexplained fall in the share price may reflect information our documents do not contain.
Tariff and trade policy uncertainty could raise costs and erode the gross margin gains of the second quarter.
Urology growth was relatively flat, and procurement pressure in China may spread beyond the stone franchise.
Street estimates sit on adjusted EPS, which excludes charges that are large in the reported accounts.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue grew from $11.9B in FY21 to $20.1B in FY25, and growth quickened every year to +19.9% in FY25. Operating margin widened from 10.1% to 18.0% over the same period, with a dip in FY24. Diluted EPS reached $1.94 in FY25.

The second quarter of 2026 added to the margin gains. Gross margin rose to 70.7% from 67.7% a year earlier, which the 10-Q attributes primarily to "increased sales of higher margin products, the benefit recognized in connection with the recovery of previously incurred tariffs and a decrease in inventory charges". SG&A and R&D expenses were both lower as a percentage of net sales than a year earlier. Operating income was $1,178 million against $819 million, an operating margin of 21.6%.

Net income attributable to common stockholders rose 13.8% to $907 million, an increase the 10-Q says was "primarily driven by higher net sales". The income statement also shows "Other, net" moving from income of $213 million to an expense of $23 million, which kept net income growth well below operating income growth. Over the six months to June 30, reported diluted EPS of $1.51 against $0.98 includes "a discrete tax benefit recorded in the first quarter of 2026", so the half-year GAAP growth overstates the trend.

The company also reports adjusted EPS, a non-GAAP measure: $0.86 in the quarter against $0.75. The 10-Q says its adjusted measures "exclude certain charges and/or credits" reported in GAAP net income "for purposes of assessing operating performance", and it lists amortization expense among the expenses management excludes. The release's full list of exclusions sits outside our excerpt; it names intangible asset impairment, acquisition-related, restructuring and restructuring-related, and litigation-related charges among the items it is "unable to predict with reasonable certainty". Second-quarter adjusted net income of $1,275 million, set beside reported net income, shows the exclusions are large, so we use GAAP figures for the record and treat adjusted EPS only as the basis of Street estimates and guidance.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
At December 31, 2025, the end of FY25, the company held $2.0B of cash and short-term investments against total debt of $11.4B, leaving net debt of $9.5B, and total equity was $24.5B. The trailing-twelve-month line puts net debt at 2.2x EBITDA and interest coverage at 11.4x. Second-quarter 2026 interest expense was $96 million against $90 million a year earlier. We read this leverage as comfortable for a business with the cash generation described below.

Liquidity is tighter than at year-end: the current ratio was 1.62 at FY25 and is 1.24 on the trailing-twelve-month line. Our figures include no quarter-end cash or debt balance, so we cannot show what moved it. The July 29 release lists both the completed accelerated share repurchase and the MiRus investment among its second-quarter results and recent developments, and each required cash. The restructuring reserve balance fell to $33 million at June 30, 2026 from $59 million at December 31, 2025.

The balance sheet does not constrain the thesis today. The question is whether further deals, including the MiRus TAVR option, would add debt while growth slows.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow rose from $1.9B in FY21 to $4.5B in FY25, and free cash flow from $1.3B to $3.7B, as the FCF margin widened to 18.2%. Capital expenditure stayed between $0.6B and $0.9B a year, so most of the gain in operating cash flow reached free cash flow. At the current price the trailing free cash flow yield is 5.9%.

The company pays no dividend. The vendor's cash flow table shows no repurchases in FY21 and FY22 and no figure for FY23 to FY25; the 2026 buyback is covered under capital allocation.

The record supports the view that this business converts earnings to cash. The counter-case is that FY25 cash flow came in a year of much faster revenue growth than the company now guides to, and slower growth will test whether the FCF margin holds.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $42.26 the shares trade on 17.1x trailing earnings, 13.2x trailing EV/EBITDA and 2.9x sales. The trailing figure lines up with reported diluted EPS over the four quarters to June 30, 2026, a window that includes the discrete tax benefit of early 2026, so the multiple looks lower than it would on earnings without that benefit.

The forward multiples sit on a different basis. The vendor's 13.0x "NTM" P/E lines up with the FY26 consensus EPS of $3.26, so it is in effect a current-year multiple, and the 12.4x figure lines up with the FY27 consensus of $3.40. The FY26 consensus sits close to, and just below, the company's July 29, 2026 guidance for 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.28 to $3.32, so we read the consensus figures as adjusted, non-GAAP estimates, on the definition set out in the financials section.

The Street is more positive than we are. Of 31 analysts, 25 rate the shares Buy, 6 Hold and none Sell. The consensus target is $60.62 and the median $60.00, within a range of $44.00 to $94.00, so even the lowest target sits above the current price. Our data does not date these targets, and some may predate part of the fall in the shares.

That fall frames every multiple here: the 52-week range runs from $41.94 to $105.65, and the price sits near the bottom of it. A low multiple on consensus earnings is attractive only if consensus holds, and the risks section explains why we cannot rule out that it will not.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Third-quarter results land within or above guidance, Electrophysiology and WATCHMAN trends steady, and the market moves to the Street's median target of $60.00. The price is a Street figure rather than our own multiple, and it would still sit well below the 52-week high.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Consensus holds: FY27 EPS of $3.40 at 13.0x, the current-year multiple the market pays today, rolled forward a year. Growth follows the company's July 29 guidance and the multiple neither expands nor contracts.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Electrophysiology competition and the WATCHMAN deceleration persist, FY27 EPS stalls at the FY26 consensus of $3.26 instead of rising, and the multiple compresses to 10x, our assumption for a device maker with little earnings growth. Both earnings and the multiple sit below the Base.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Each weight rests on evidence about FY27, the year all three anchors depend on.

The Base carries 55%. It asks little of the company: consensus already expects only modest earnings growth in FY27, as the growth section shows. Keeping today's multiple is the neutral assumption when nothing in our documents points to either a further derating or a recovery.

The Bear carries 25%. In its favor, the 10-Q reports the Electrophysiology competition discussed under risks, and third-quarter guidance points to a slowdown from the second quarter. Against it, the accelerated share repurchase has cut the share count, which supports EPS even if net income stalls, the second quarter showed the cost discipline noted in the financials section, and the new restructuring program may lower costs. A flat FY27 is plausible but not the central outcome.

The Bull carries 20%, less than the Bear. It needs FY27 earnings to meet consensus and the market to pay a much higher multiple for them within a year, yet more than two months after results that met or beat guidance the price sits near its 52-week low. Clinical results and the Street's ratings support it; the company's near-term outlook, which slows into the third quarter, does not yet.

These weights give a probability-weighted fair value of $44.46, expected upside of +5.2%, bear-case downside of -22.9% and reward/risk of 0.23×. The label does not hinge on the split: swapping the Bull and Bear weights still leaves expected upside short of the BUY line. The call is more sensitive to the share price than to the weights, which the final recommendation addresses.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Our data vendor shows only a consolidated total and treats the company as a single segment, while the 10-Q MD&A and the July 29 release present net sales by two reportable segments, MedSurg and Cardiovascular; we use the company's presentation. In the second quarter of 2026, Cardiovascular net sales grew 8.3% on a reported basis. MedSurg grew 5.9%: Neuromodulation rose 12.7%, Endoscopy 7.6% and Urology 1.1%. The mix leans toward the faster-growing Cardiovascular segment, so the company's growth depends most on how that segment performs.

moatFactors.name: Clinical evidence and approvals
moatFactors.body: Device sales depend on clinical data and regulatory clearance, and the company keeps producing both. The July 29 release reports that the AVANT GUARD study "demonstrated statistical superiority of FARAPULSE PFA over anti-arrhythmic drugs", and that the FRACTURE trial "met its primary endpoints"; it also reports a 510(k) clearance for the TruSelect 2.6 Microcatheter. The 10-K risk factors, filed February 17, 2026, count the need to "obtain required regulatory and reimbursement approvals" among the demands of competing. The same 10-K adds that launch delays and "the overall performance of, and continued physician confidence in," next-generation products "may result in declines in our market share", so the advantage has to be renewed product by product.

moatFactors.name: Gross margin stability
moatFactors.body: Gross margin held between 68.6% and 69.5% from FY21 to FY25 while revenue grew every year, and it stands at 69.9% on a trailing-twelve-month basis, which points to pricing that has held across the portfolio. The 10-K warns of "national and regional government tenders" and pressure on average selling prices, and the 10-Q reports volume-based procurement in China weighing on the stone franchise, so the pricing strength is not uniform.

moatFactors.name: R&D scale and breadth
moatFactors.body: R&D expenses were $554 million in the second quarter of 2026, or 10.2% of net sales, spent, in the 10-Q's words, "to maintain a pipeline of products that we believe will contribute to future sales growth". Four businesses spread the risk of any one product. The 10-K counters that "some of our competitors may have greater financial and marketing resources than we do" and that developments by other companies, "including low-cost alternatives, may make our products or proposed products obsolete or less competitive".

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. The case for an advantage rests on the margin record and clinical programs described above, and on an operating margin that has reached 19.8% on a trailing basis. The case against comes from the company's own filings: the 10-Q reports rising competition in Electrophysiology, and the 10-K describes markets that are "highly competitive" and "characterized by extensive research and development and rapid technological change". A wide rating would need evidence that the company can hold its position in Electrophysiology as competition increases, and the latest filing points the other way. Durability over the next few years depends on whether the investigational products discussed under growth reach the market and sell.

points: Guidance implies a slower second half. On July 29, 2026 the company said it "now estimates" full-year 2026 net sales growth of approximately 5.5 to 6.5 percent reported and 5 to 6 percent organic, after organic growth of 8.1% in the six months to June 30. Its third-quarter outlook is approximately 3 to 5 percent on a reported and organic basis.

The Street expects the slowdown to last. Consensus revenue of $21.2B (+6%) for FY26 sits inside the company's range, and $22.3B for FY27 implies a pace far below the FY25 acceleration covered in the financials section. Consensus EPS of $3.40 for FY27 is only modestly above the $3.26 expected for FY26.

Cardiovascular carries the growth and the pressure. The 10-Q credits the segment's second-quarter growth primarily to its coronary therapies franchise, led by the AGENT Drug-Coated Balloon, and to its Electrophysiology business unit, led by Farapulse. The competition and WATCHMAN deceleration the 10-Q reports in the same segment, discussed under risks, limit how much of that growth we carry into FY27.

Neuromodulation and Endoscopy add breadth. The 10-Q credits Neuromodulation's growth primarily to its pain portfolio, led by the Intracept Intraosseous Nerve Ablation System and the Nalu Peripheral Nerve Stimulation System, and to deep brain stimulation, and Endoscopy's to its biliary franchise, led by the AXIOS Stent and Delivery System, and its core GI franchise. Both are smaller than Cardiovascular, so they cushion rather than replace it.

The pipeline is optionality, not a support for FY27. The release lists the FARAFLEX Mapping and PFA Catheter, now enrolling in the pivotal FARADIGM trial, the SEISMIQ 4CE Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy Catheter and the SIEGEL TAVR system as investigational and "Not available for sale". With no launch dates in our documents, we give them no weight in FY27 earnings.

management.leadership: The July 29, 2026 release names Mike Mahoney as chairman and chief executive officer; the proxy excerpt of March 18, 2026 calls Mr. Mahoney "our President and Chief Executive Officer". His comment on the quarter was measured, describing "a solid quarter while continuing to navigate a dynamic environment" and a focus on "disciplined execution and prioritizing investments in our highest-impact opportunities". Delivery in the quarter matched the words: reported growth of 7.5% reached the top of the 5.5 to 7.5 percent guidance range, organic growth of 7.0% the top of the 5 to 7 percent range, and adjusted EPS of $0.86 beat the $0.82 to $0.84 range. The counterweight is the outlook management set at the same time, which slows into the third quarter even as it voices confidence in "long-term growth". On this quarter's evidence the team guides accurately; the next two quarters will show whether the slower outlook is conservative or a sign of lost momentum.
management.capitalAllocation:
Recent capital has gone to a buyback, a minority stake and restructuring rather than dividends. The July 29, 2026 release reports completion of the previously announced $2 billion accelerated share repurchase, which retired approximately 40 million shares, and diluted weighted-average shares fell to 1,474.8 million in the second quarter from 1,493.5 million a year earlier. The release gives no average purchase price, so we cannot judge the buyback's return against today's price. The company also invested $1.5 billion in MiRus LLC for an approximately 34% equity stake and an exclusive option to acquire the MiRus TAVR business; that buys a position in a company whose TAVR system is not yet for sale.

On July 21, 2026 the Board approved a new global restructuring program. It follows the 2023 Restructuring Plan, which the 10-Q calls "substantially complete" with $748 million of cumulative pre-tax charges, inside its estimated total of approximately $700 million to $800 million. The excerpt gives no cost or savings figure for the new program, and restructuring charges sit among the items adjusted EPS guidance excludes. We see the buyback as supportive of per-share earnings and the MiRus stake as a reasonable but unproven bet.
management.governance: The proxy statement excerpt (DEF 14A, March 18, 2026) shows that the Board has determined that, other than Mr. Mahoney, all directors qualify as independent under NYSE standards, and that the Corporate Governance Guidelines require "a significant majority" of independent directors. The July 29 release names Mr. Mahoney chairman as well as chief executive, so the two roles are combined; the excerpt does not show whether the Board has a lead independent director. Related party transactions fall under a written policy overseen by the Nominating and Governance Committee, with the General Counsel identifying potential transactions and providing an annual summary; the policy covers transactions above the SEC disclosure threshold, generally $120,000. The excerpt carries no executive pay detail, so we make no claim about pay design. For shareholders, a board that is independent apart from the chief executive and a written related-party process are a sound base, and the combined chair and chief executive role is the point we would want the full proxy to address.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt we draw on contains no beneficial ownership table, so we make no statement about how much stock directors and officers hold.

idiosyncratic: Electrophysiology and WATCHMAN. The 10-Q says net sales in the second quarter and first half "were impacted by increased competition within our Electrophysiology business unit and a deceleration of certain WATCHMAN procedures". Electrophysiology is one of the two business units the 10-Q credits with growth, so share loss there would hit the larger segment first. The third-quarter report is the next evidence on whether the pressure is deepening.

An unexplained fall. None of the excerpts we draw on, from the 10-Q, the July 29 release, the 10-K and the proxy statement, gives a reason for the decline in the share price. The market may be pricing information these documents do not contain, including anything that followed the 10-Q of August 3, 2026. If the market's caution proves right, consensus earnings may be too high, and so would our Base, which rests on them.

Adjusted versus reported earnings. Guidance and Street estimates sit on adjusted EPS, and the gap to reported earnings set out in the financials section is wide. The new restructuring program is likely to add charges that fall outside the adjusted figure, so an investor who values the company on reported earnings pays a higher multiple than the forward P/E suggests.

Urology and procurement. The 10-Q attributes Urology's "relatively flat" growth primarily to "underperformance in our stone franchise as a result of volume-based-procurement in China" and to commercial disruption in sacral neuromodulation. The 10-K warns that local procurement processes "may favor local players to multinational companies like us", so the pressure could reach other products.
risks.systemic:
Trade policy is the systemic risk the 10-Q stresses. It describes "significant uncertainty with respect to global trade policies, including changing tariff rates", which "could adversely impact our operations and results", and says the company "may also experience higher distribution costs and supply chain disruptions". Part of the second-quarter gross margin gain came from the tariff recovery noted in the financials section, and it may not recur.

Across the industry, the 10-K risk factors filed February 17, 2026 point to consolidation among customers, government tenders and shifts in sites of care that "may impact procedure volumes, product mix, and pricing and contracting". These are slow-moving pressures, while tariffs are the one that could move margins within a year.

body: We rate Boston Scientific HOLD with a target range of $40.00 to $47.00, which brackets our Base of $44.20 and our weighted fair value. For a holder, a weighted value close to the price and a bear case well below it argue for neither adding nor selling. For a buyer, the Street's more positive view is the opposing case, and we would need a lower price or better third-quarter evidence to share it.

With our scenarios unchanged, the label moves with the price: at the bottom of our range the page's math derives BUY, and at the top it derives SELL. We will revisit the scenarios themselves on the third-quarter report. Organic growth at or above the top of the company's third-quarter range, with the full-year adjusted EPS range held or raised, would move weight from Bear to Bull. Growth below the range, or a cut to the full-year EPS range, would put the FY27 consensus behind our Base at risk and lower our weighted value.
